pick.headline: Man fires at Gorbachev's parade on Red Square
pick.summary: On November 7, 1990, during the revolution anniversary parade, a Leningrad man fired a shotgun toward the reviewing stand on Red Square where Mikhail Gorbachev stood. He was overpowered and nobody was hit.
pick.significance: The attempt on the Soviet leader's life underlined how far the country's tensions had come into the open in the last year of the USSR.
pick.fbis: TASS in English reported the same day that several shots rang through Red Square during the official anniversary celebrations; FBIS ran it in that day's Soviet Union report.

alternates.headline: Ben Ali removes Bourguiba in Tunisia
alternates.summary: On November 7, 1987, Prime Minister Zine El Abidine Ben Ali had doctors declare President Habib Bourguiba unfit to rule and took power in Tunisia.
alternates.significance: The bloodless 'medical coup' ended the rule of Tunisia's founding president. Ben Ali, a former security chief, would rule until 2011.
alternates.fbis: FBIS's Near East & South Asia review reported Ben Ali replacing Bourguiba as president and supreme commander after Bourguiba was declared "totally incapable", citing the new leader's statement broadcast by Tunis radio.
